A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic planning, Countdown, Sudoku and SAT, together with ablations, scaling, decoding-speed and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on token-reweighted autoregressive training and combined data/model scaling in Appendix D.

M1.justification: MDM is renamed MGDM, with 'Mask' added to its expanded name in the abstract. The absorbing-mask diffusion procedure, weighted objective in Equation 8, TopK decoding and Algorithms 1-2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate minimal planning, Countdown 3-5, Game of 24, Sudoku and SAT with 5, 7 and 9 variables. The added appendix experiments use existing tasks; the larger training sample changes experimental scale rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2/Table 7 adds an AR variant using the token-reweighting mechanism from Equation 8 as a control on minimal planning. The original AR, reverse-AR, teacherless and benchmark comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3/Table 8 adds a 303M-parameter, one-million-training-example configuration to the Countdown comparison, extending the existing 500k-example settings. Appendix D.2 also introduces the AR reweighting control. The original experiments' splits, metrics and stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Two focused analyses are added: whether token reweighting resolves AR's difficult planning subgoals, and how increasing data alongside model size affects performance. Existing diffusion ablations, convergence plots, speed analysis, error analysis and prediction case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 retains the same statement that experiments were run multiple times and statistical significance was verified. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures are supplied for the added results; existing uncertainty displays are retained.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports reweighted-AR accuracies of 52.1%, 51.5%, 50.3% and 51.9% at planning distances 2-5. New Table 8 adds 53.3% for AR and 95.6% for MGDM at 303M parameters with 1M training examples. These are additional results under added configurations; the corresponding original main-table results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 replaces v1's assertion that tokens need not follow their data-distribution autoregressive conditionals with a statement that subgoal learning difficulty depends on model parameterization. AR factorization is then discussed separately. This is a localized substantive revision; the loss derivations and Appendix A mathematics are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: explaining AR difficulties through subgoal imbalance, proposing multi-granularity diffusion training, and demonstrating advantages on reasoning and planning tasks. The headline 91.5% Countdown and 100% Sudoku results and their scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly connects prioritizing difficult subgoals to prioritizing their associated denoising views. Appendix D.3 adds the interpretation that jointly scaling data and model size benefits both AR and MGDM. The regretful-compromise discussion is also refined, while its central planning-error explanation remains.

D1.justification: Appendices B-C retain the same algorithms, architecture specifications, learning rates, batch sizes, training epochs, hardware and decoding settings. The existing code-access statement moves from the introduction to the abstract with the same URL. No additional implementation instructions accompany the new experimental configurations.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged, including Appendix A's background. Replacing 'In contrast' with 'In this work' in Section 5.2 does not change the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates MDM terminology to MGDM, locally rewrites the proposition, motivation and error discussion, moves the code statement, adds acknowledgments and inserts two appendix subsections. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7-8 and relocates the existing case-study and task-example tables as Tables 9-10. Figure and table labels adopt MGDM, hyperlinks become colored, and nearby material reflows. Existing plots and table designs are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added AR-reweighting control tests whether weighting alone explains the planning advantage, while the scaling experiment strengthens evidence about sensitivity to training-data budget. Revising Proposition 1 removes a problematic conditional-distribution assertion and improves the argument's precision. These are useful, focused improvements; the main method and empirical conclusions remain stable.
